current_topic.label: Sick-day care
current_topic.scope: Prepare ordinary essentials, familiar food and optional support before a future sick day.

input.user_context: I live alone. I have a friend I could ask, but we haven't arranged anything. I want to prepare for a future sick day.
reviewed_guidance: Ordinary preventive organization and personal choices only. Do not provide medical treatment, hazardous DIY or guarantees of protection.

tasks.title: Set up a sick-day shelf
tasks.summary: A few everyday essentials within reach when you need to rest. Start with what you already have.
steps: Choose a reachable shelf or basket near where you usually rest.
Gather tissues, a charging cable and other everyday essentials you already use.
Note one missing item for your next usual shopping trip.
tasks.done_when: Your available essentials are together, with any missing item noted.

tasks.title: Choose two easy meals
tasks.summary: A short meal list gives you fewer decisions to make on a lower-energy day.
steps: Choose two familiar meals you find easy to prepare.
Check which ingredients you already have.
Save the meal names and any missing ingredients in one note.
tasks.done_when: Two meal options and any missing ingredients are saved in one note.

tasks.title: Draft a check-in request
tasks.summary: Keep a message ready so asking for company takes less effort when you want it.
steps: Choose the friend you would like to ask.
Write: “I'm feeling unwell. Would you have time for a short check-in tomorrow?”
Save the draft somewhere you can find it.
tasks.done_when: Your draft is saved with the intended person's name.

critique_notes: The three outcomes are reachable essentials, meal options and a saved request; each is independently usable.
A missing-item note is not a required purchase; avoid_spending remains respected.
The friend is explicitly supplied as someone the person could ask, not an already-agreed helper.
The tasks prepare for a future sick day; they are not medical guidance for a current illness.
No resource is attached because the actions are self-contained and no eligible resource was supplied.
The shelf example preserves the approved layout and familiar idea; wording remains a proposed calibration example.
